answer: Output deduplication punishes cloned work rather than cloned identities alone. Each completed task is hashed at submission into one public vault, where every accepted result becomes a numbered pearl; near-identical hashes under two identities are flagged automatically. Detection is cheap because similarity search scales sublinearly, while the attacker pays twice: to generate the work, then as a slashed onyx stake per submission once a duplicate appears. Copying across many identities costs as much as doing distinct tasks, removing the economic reason to multiply agents.
